title: Finite Q3 Gibbs modular-band identity and similarity-factor stress
question: For finite Q3 Gibbs states rho_beta proportional to exp(-beta H), can the modular similarity rho_beta^(-1/2) Delta rho_beta^(1/2) be represented exactly in the H eigenbasis and bounded by the finite energy-band factor, and how does that factor stress the uniformity gate?
method: Construct the canonical finite Q3 Hamiltonians on volume 2 and volume 4 with oscillator dimension three, and volume 6 with oscillator dimension two, using chi=1, r=-1, g=3/5, c=3/5 and lambda=1/10.
For beta in the declared five-point sweep and both cutoff radii, form the normalized Gibbs spectrum p_i=exp(-beta(E_i-E_min))/Z and the full/local shifted energy weights.
Transform the direct matrices rho^(-1/2) Delta rho^(1/2) and rho^(1/2) Delta rho^(-1/2) into the H eigenbasis and compare them with the explicit diagonal spectral formulas.

Check the finite operator-norm energy-band envelope with factor exp(beta(E_max-E_min)/2), the analogous local/full K envelope, and the corresponding source-boundary history rows for both orientations and interpolation values.
Run the non-importing independent reconstruction, compare coefficient and history rows, compile and registry-check Lean R345, and retain all common-core and QFT promotion gates as open.
finding: The primary lane passes 922/922 assertions and the non-importing independent lane passes 922/922; the integrated verifier passes 18/18 with Lean R345 PASS. There are 60 coefficient rows and 720 history rows. The largest direct spectral-identity residual is 2.09551902400554e-7 under the separately declared 1e-6 finite conditioning tolerance. The Gibbs energy-band factor ranges from 1.1850038335904713 to 11115.995140263556 across the declared beta/volume/cutoff scenarios; representative volume-4, dimension-3, beta-2, radius-0.5 rows have band factor 11115.995140263556 and Gibbs similarity norm 116.167425341673 for tail norm 9. The finite history envelope ratios range from 3.66711896042345e-16 to 0.0750654451645886.
decision_reason: The eigenbasis calculation makes the modular multiplier cost explicit: finite Gibbs inverse powers insert an energy-band factor that is harmless on each bounded matrix but can become very large with beta and spectral width. The exact finite identity and conservative norm envelope are reusable QFT-facing bookkeeping, while the observed band growth and the conditioning-sensitive residual prevent any claim of beta-, volume- or cutoff-uniform modular-domain control. This is a route-local stress boundary, not a global no-go theorem.

adversarial_review.check: The partition function cancels only in the band ratio; the normalized finite Gibbs matrix and its rank are independently constructed for every row.
Both modular orientations and both source signs are compared with their H-eigenbasis formulas, so one-sided modular control is not substituted.
The band envelope is derived from submultiplicativity and is checked against direct norms; no entrywise bound is promoted to an unproved Schur-multiplier estimate.
The maximum identity residual is retained and covered by a separately declared 1e-6 finite tolerance; this tolerance is not called a physical or uniform error estimate.
The factor exp(beta(E_max-E_min)/2) is reported across the full declared sweep, and its growth is treated as a route-local stress rather than a global divergence theorem.
Local K_X and full K bands are kept separate and neither finite shift is identified with the infinite-volume modular generator.
The independent lane rebuilds the Q3 model, Gibbs spectra, cutoff bonds, spectral identities and history rows without importing the primary audit.
R345 certifies the ordered-field exponential band inequality only; matrix spectral calculus, inverse-power conditioning and all QFT limits remain Python evidence/open analysis.

This finite spectral checkpoint does not prove modular-domain transfer, common-core uniformity, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, a common OS carrier, exhaustion, common alpha, Hamiltonian-OS identification, a GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.

qft_interface.open: The energy-band factor is beta- and spectral-width-dependent; uniform control on an unbounded common core, modular-domain transfer, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, products, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
